hypothesis: H67-APFL: Blind alluvial piedmont faults under Qal alluvium produce coincident LiDAR sub-metre step (L_step_max), DEM TPI11 flexure and crest ridge, isostatic gravity analytic-signal gradient, depth-to-basement thickening gradient, and conductivity clay-pan edge; product detector S = L_valid·(L_step^0.35·gravAS^0.30·depthGrad^0.20·condGrad^0.05·TPI_pos^0.10)·(1+0.5·crest) with p1-p99 scaling, ridge-NMS and 300 m score-ordered thinning with tip-preserved flank shield r=2.5 px.
mechanism: Catalogue-free hand-crafted product emphasizes co-located surface warp (LiDAR+DEM) and basement step (gravity+depth) to find buried basin-margin faults systematically missing from QFFDB/INGENIOUS (Stahl & Niemi 2017). Ridge-NMS extracts lineaments, score-ordered Poisson-disk thins to 43,798 dots at min_dist=3.0 px, flank shield removes 50,810 non-tip lateral apron ridges within 2.5 px of visible faults while preserving 2,532 tip relays.
mimicking_non_fault_process: Unfaulted alluvial-fan depositional onlap wedges, axial drainage incision, and aeolian deflation surfaces also produce TPI/gravity/depth gradients; modern Qal fan toes thicken basinward without fault. Mimic differentiated by gravity polarity + LiDAR step coincidence vs pure depositional thickening (requires gravity step).
